items.title: Iran hangs two more protesters as execution wave accelerates

featured_image.name: Iranian protesters clash with security forces as tear gas fills Tehran  streets amid nationwide unrest

items.description: Iran carried out two more executions on Sunday, hanging Mohammadamin Biglari, 19, and Shahin Vahedparast in connection with the January 2026 protests, the judiciary's Mizan Online website announced. The executions bring to at least twelve the number of political prisoners and protesters put to death since March 19, as the Islamic Republic accelerates a campaign of capital punishment against those who took part in the nationwide uprising that erupted in late December 2025.[1][2]

items.title: Saudi, Egypt PMIs contract sharply as war chokes demand

featured_image.name: Saudi non-oil private sector soars to 60.2 in October on ...

items.description: The Middle East conflict is taking a mounting toll on the region's two largest economies, with closely watched business surveys released Sunday showing that non-oil private sector activity in both Egypt and Saudi Arabia contracted sharply in March.

items.title: Ukraine drone strike damages oil pipeline at Russia's Primorsk port

featured_image.name: Russia's top oil terminal lost 40% of storage in Ukraine drone attacks

items.description:
A Ukrainian drone attack damaged an oil pipeline near Russia's Baltic Sea port of Primorsk overnight on Sunday, the latest in a sustained campaign that has crippled the country's northwestern oil export infrastructure for more than two weeks.

Leningrad Oblast Governor Alexander Drozdenko said on Telegram that Russian air defenses intercepted 19 drones over the region, but debris from one "damaged a section of the oil pipeline near the port of Primorsk, and the pipeline is being safely burned out." He said there were no casualties, and the pipeline was shut down while the fire was allowed to safely burn out.[1][2][3][4]

items.title: Pakistan presses Iran, Egypt, Bahrain on ceasefire amid US-Iran war

featured_image.name: Will China join Pakistan-led efforts to mediate US-Iran ...

items.description: As the war between the United States and Iran enters its sixth week with no ceasefire in sight, Egypt and Pakistan have emerged as central diplomatic players, conducting back-channel shuttle diplomacy aimed at bringing Washington and Tehran to the negotiating table.

items.title: Fires hit Abu Dhabi's Borouge plant after Iranian attack

featured_image.name: UAE's Borouge to award EPC contract for EU2 ethane cracker ...

items.description:
Abu Dhabi authorities on Sunday responded to multiple fires at the Borouge petrochemicals plant in Ruwais after falling debris from air defence interceptions struck the facility, the Associated Press reported. Operations at the plant have been suspended while an assessment of the damage is underway, with the Abu Dhabi Media Office confirming that no injuries have been reported.[1][2]

The plant, located near the UAE's western border with Saudi Arabia, is part of the sprawling Ruwais Industrial Complex operated by Abu Dhabi National Oil Company and is set to become the world's largest single-site polyolefins complex.[3]

items.title: Iran fires missiles at Israel, Kuwait after Trump ultimatum

featured_image.name: Trump: U.S. will bomb Iran "back to stone ages" over next 2-3 weeks

items.description: Iran launched missiles and drones at Israel and Kuwait early Sunday, one day after President Donald Trump warned Tehran it had 48 hours to reach a deal or reopen the Strait of Hormuz before "all Hell will reign down on them." Kuwait and Israel said their air defenses were responding to the latest barrage, according to AFP, as the war that began February 28 entered its 37th day with no end in sight.[1][2]

items.title: Pope Leo XIV leads first Easter Vigil with plea for peace

featured_image.name: TOPSHOT-VATICAN-RELIGION-EASTER-VIGIL

items.description: Pope Leo XIV presided over his first Easter Vigil as pontiff on Saturday evening at St. Peter's Basilica, delivering a homily that urged the world not to grow numb to war and called on the faithful to help the "Easter gifts of harmony and peace" take root across the globe.[1][2]

items.title: Pope Leo XIV to deliver first Urbi et Orbi amid war critique

featured_image.name: Pope Leo's official portrait breaks conventions in papal ...

items.description: Pope Leo XIV has used the solemn liturgies of Holy Week to deliver a sustained rebuke of those who invoke Christianity to justify military action, drawing a sharp contrast with U.S. Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth's calls to pray for battlefield triumph "in the name of Jesus Christ."

items.title: Pope Leo XIV celebrates Easter Mass at the Vatican

featured_image.name: At Easter vigil, Pope urges peace in world torn by war

items.description: Christians around the world are marking Easter Sunday on April 5, 2026, with religious services, community gatherings, and festive celebrations commemorating the resurrection of Jesus Christ.

items.title: Western carriers seize routes as Iran war guts Gulf aviation hubs

featured_image.name: Western airlines seize market share as Iran war disrupts Middle East aviation hubs

items.description: More than five weeks after the United States and Israel launched strikes on Iran on February 28, the war has upended the global aviation industry, shuttering Middle Eastern airspace, grounding tens of thousands of flights, and opening a rare window for Western and Turkish carriers to capture traffic long dominated by Gulf airlines.

items.title: Iranian drones hit Kuwait government, oil buildings in latest Gulf strikes

featured_image.name: Kuwait.. Four Drones Shot Down in Various Areas of the Country

items.description: Kuwait, Saudi Arabia, Bahrain, and other Persian Gulf nations endured another wave of Iranian drone and missile attacks over the weekend, as the US-Israeli military campaign against Iran stretches into its sixth week with no end in sight.

items.title: U.S. forces rescue second F-15E crew member from Iran after firefight

featured_image.name: A US F-15 is down in Iran, search and rescue underway

items.description:
U.S. military forces successfully extracted the second crew member of an F-15E Strike Eagle that was shot down over Iran on Friday, capping a tense rescue operation that stretched more than 24 hours and involved firefights with Iranian forces on the ground, according to U.S. officials cited by The Wall Street Journal.[1]

The weapons systems officer had been evading capture in southwestern Iran while Iranian military units and local militia forces combed the area, with Iranian state media broadcasting a bounty of roughly $60,000 for anyone who located the American airmen, according to the BBC. U.S. special operations forces reached the WSO and extracted him in what journalist Jack Murphy, a former Green Beret, described as a "massive firefight" at the recovery site. Al Jazeera reported that a U.S. government representative confirmed the second crew member had been "retrieved" after an "intense exchange of gunfire".[2][3][4][5][6]

items.title: Israel strikes Iran's petrochemical zone as US pilot search continues

featured_image.name: Iran War Live: Race To Find Missing Airman, Tehran Offers Reward

items.description: U.S. and Israeli warplanes struck Iran's Mahshahr Special Petrochemical Zone on Saturday, killing at least five people and wounding 170 others according to Iranian state media, as the search for a missing American crew member whose fighter jet was shot down the previous day stretched into a second day.[1][2]

items.title: Iran rejects Trump's 48-hour ultimatum as Gulf strikes widen

featured_image.name: Kuwait desalination plant, oil refinery hit by missile and drone strikes

items.description:
Iran's central military command on Saturday dismissed President Donald Trump's 48-hour ultimatum to reopen the Strait of Hormuz or face the destruction of its critical infrastructure, as Tehran continued launching waves of drone and missile strikes across the Gulf and at Israel in the latest escalation of the five-week-old war.

General Ali Abdollahi Aliabadi, representing Iran's Khatam al-Anbiya Central Headquarters, called Trump's threat "a helpless, nervous, unbalanced and stupid action," and warned: "The simple meaning of this message is that the gates of hell will open for you." Trump had written on Truth Social earlier Saturday: "Time is running out — 48 hours before all Hell will reign down on them. Glory be to GOD!"[1][2][3]

items.title: Meloni offers to help rebuild Qatar's war-damaged gas infrastructure

featured_image.name: Italy's Meloni meets Qatar emir to discuss energy issues amid Iran war

items.description:
Italian Prime Minister Giorgia Meloni met with Qatari Emir Sheikh Tamim bin Hamad Al Thani at Lusail Palace in Doha on Saturday, offering Italy's support to rebuild Qatar's damaged energy infrastructure as Europe grapples with an energy crisis triggered by the US-Israeli war on Iran.[1][2]

Meloni is the first leader from the European Union, NATO, and the G20 to visit the Gulf region since the conflict began on February 28. The unannounced two-day tour, which started in Saudi Arabia on Friday with a meeting with Crown Prince Mohammed bin Salman, will also include the United Arab Emirates.[3][4][5]

items.title: Iran's military warns Israeli embassies are 'legitimate targets'

featured_image.name: Iran's Khatam al-Anbiya Headquarters details Waves 91 & 92 of “Al-Waad  Al-Sadiq 4”

items.description: Iran's top military command issued a stark warning on Saturday that any Israeli attack on Iranian embassies or diplomatic facilities would prompt retaliatory strikes on Israeli diplomatic sites across the Middle East, escalating rhetoric amid an ongoing military conflict between Iran and a US-Israeli coalition.

items.title: Iran's grip on Strait of Hormuz fuels growing recession fears worldwide

featured_image.name: The Oil Shock Is Here. And We're Just Beginning to Feel It.

items.description: A grinding war in Iran and the effective closure of the Strait of Hormuz have sent oil prices surging and rattled financial markets worldwide, intensifying fears that the global economy may be headed for a recession. With crude benchmarks trading well above $100 a barrel and bond yields falling, Wall Street is signaling that the risk of economic contraction now outweighs concerns about inflation.

items.title: Trump warns Iran of 'hell' as search for downed jet crew enters day 2

featured_image.name: Trump says Iran has 48 hours to make deal as search for US pilot continues

items.description: President Donald Trump dismissed the loss of an American F-15E Strike Eagle fighter jet over Iran on Friday, telling NBC News in a phone interview that the incident would have no bearing on ongoing diplomatic efforts with Tehran. "No, not at all. No, it's war. We're in war, Garrett," Trump told NBC News correspondent Garrett Haake, in his first public remarks on the shootdown.[1][2][3]

items.title: Trump aides advise striking Iran's infrastructure as Monday deadline nears

featured_image.name: Trump extends pause on attacking Iran energy facilities to April 6

items.description:
Senior Trump administration officials have privately advised President Donald Trump that striking Iran's energy and power infrastructure constitutes a legitimate military target, according to The Wall Street Journal, as the U.S.-Iran war enters its sixth week with a critical deadline just two days away.[1][2]

The reporting comes as Trump's self-imposed April 6 deadline for Iran to reopen the Strait of Hormuz or reach a deal approaches on Monday evening. On Saturday, Trump reiterated his ultimatum on Truth Social, warning that "all hell" would rain down on Iran if it fails to comply within 48 hours.[3][4]

items.title: Israel warns it will strike Lebanon-Syria border crossing

featured_image.name: Key Lebanon–Syria border crossing destroyed by Israeli attack

items.description: The Israel Defense Forces carried out simultaneous waves of strikes across Iran and Lebanon over the weekend, hitting more than 200 Iranian targets and over 140 Hezbollah positions as the five-week-old Operation Roaring Lion continued to expand in scope. The IDF also confirmed the death of another soldier in southern Lebanon, bringing the toll to 11 since ground operations began on March 16.[1][2][3]
